svg.title: Reduced cotangent fibres and quadratic Morse tests
svg.desc: The actual dual-number tangent of a cotangent pullback includes the Hessian B of the fixed output covector composed with the map. A zero fibre tangent makes its projection injective. The image is isotropic, so a symmetric target graph can be chosen transverse to it. The pulled-back Hessian B plus transpose F Q F is then transverse to the smooth Lagrangian source component. For an actual bounded conormal model, the normalized cycle is the coefficient tensored with its degree-zero Morse orientation line, with monodromy minus one to the source-stratum dimension. Quadratic ramification has a reduced fibre and a Morse test; cubic ramification has a length-two fibre and a non-Morse but still nonzero cycle. The open bounded Hecke fibre comparison retains all coefficient-ring residue equations and the opposite bound.
svg.text: Reduced cotangent fibres and quadratic Morse tests
Smooth Lagrangian source component; actual scheme fibres; characteristic zero.
1. Keep the full changing cotangent pullback — RTM.1–RTM.7
F=df, B=Hess(η f), L=tangent of the source component.
E = { (v,α) : (v,Fᵗα+Bv) lies in L }, dq(v,α)=(Fv,α).
Zero tangent of the fibre ⇒ dq on E is injective.
Symmetry of B cancels its two terms in the symplectic pairing.
W=dq(E) is isotropic, so dim W ≤ dim Y.
2. Choose the target graph; retain the source Hessian — RTM.8–RTM.15
Choose symmetric Q with W ∩ graph(Q) = 0.
g(z)=ηz+½Q(z,z), h=g f, Hess h = B+Fᵗ Q F.
(v,Hess h ·v) in L ⇒ (Fv,QFv)=0 ⇒ v=0.
The source graph is transverse; finitely many such conditions can be imposed.
On a conormal T*ₛX this is exactly a nondegenerate critical point of h on S.
3. The bounded local coefficient has an exact degree — RTM.16–RTM.21
For the actual model j_* Mₛ[d], d=dim(S):
Covered quadratic fibre retracts to S^(d−1), with its constant-section unit.
Normalized Φₕ(j_* Mₛ[d]) at x = M ⊗ Morse orientation line.
The line is in degree zero; its monodromy is (−1)^d.
The d=0 case has empty nearby fibre and identity monodromy.
4. Equal reduced supports do not give equal fibre hypotheses — RTM.24–RTM.28
t=z², η≠0: fibre k[z]/(2ηz)=k; B=2η gives a Morse test.
The normalized cycle is one line in degree zero, with monodromy −1.
t=z³: fibre k[z]/(3ηz²) has length two and a nonzero tangent.
F=0 and B=0: every pulled-back quadratic target test has zero Hessian.
Its isolated cycle still has dimension two; the reduced-fibre Morse claim fails.
5. A nonzero conormal and the actual Hecke fibre — RTM.22–RTM.30
f(s,t)=s+t², S={s=0}, input covector ds, output covector dy.
h on S is t²: the cycle is in degree zero and has monodromy −1.
Open Hecke orbit: residue equations force A₂ to be regular in both lattices.
Full Higgs gluing and the moving residue identify the actual coefficient-ring fibre.
The output-fixed reduced point uses the inverse modification and opposite bound.
Exact proofs: §§3.279–3.288, RTM.1–RTM.30; Solutions3.EE,3.EF,3.EG.
Generic microlocal coefficient comparison remains a separate requirement.
A bounded coefficient calculation does not prove full-category cycle exactness or completion.
Nilpotent support identification, full-image regularity and field transfer remain separate.
